title: gitbox configuration v5
description: Configuration file for gitbox — manages Git multi-account environments across multiple providers (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Bitbucket).

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI for editor validation and autocompletion.

version.description: Configuration format version. Must be 5. v2, v3 and v4 files are migrated to v5 automatically on load.

global.description: Global settings: clone roots, SSH and GCM credential configuration.

roots.description: Clone roots: the folders gitbox clones into and scans for clones. The first one is the default. A clone lives at <root>/<source folder>/<org>/<repo>. Supports ~ prefix for home directory or absolute paths.

nested_scan_depth.description: How many directory levels gitbox descends below a container repo (see repo.container) when discovering nested clones. Defaults to 1 (immediate children) when unset.

ignored_clones.description: Absolute paths of clones found under a root that you chose not to track. The disk reconcile never adopts them or lists them as unmatched.

language.description: Default language for human-facing program output. English remains the fallback when missing.

periodic_sync.description: Automatic periodic fetch interval. When set, the GUI will run 'git fetch' on all repos at this interval.

check_global_gitignore.description: Gates the automatic startup check for the recommended ~/.gitignore_global heal. An explicit click on the GUI Install button always runs regardless. Defaults to true when missing.

pr_badges_enabled.description: Whether PR and review indicators are fetched and shown on clone rows. Defaults to true when missing.

pr_include_drafts.description: Whether draft PRs count in the "my PRs" badge. Defaults to true when missing.

remote_tint.description: The color that tints the top bar and the sidebar of remote windows. Absent means the default blue. A client preference.

remotes.description: Remote-mode destinations of this machine. A client preference. Each entry names an ssh_config Host alias; gitbox stores no hostname, user or key.

alias.description: The ssh_config Host alias, resolved only by the system ssh. Unique within the list.

server_dir.description: Overrides where gitbox-server is installed on the remote, for homes mounted noexec. Absolute, or starting with ~/. Absent means the default under the home.

editor.description: Remote-capable editor command for this remote. Absent means automatic.

server_os.description: Operating system the host's server reported on the last connection, as Go spells it. Saved automatically.

server_arch.description: Architecture the host's server reported on the last connection, as Go spells it. Saved automatically.

server_version.description: Version of the host's server on the last connection. Saved automatically.

last_connected.description: When this remote's window last connected (RFC 3339). Saved automatically.

window.description: Position and size of this remote's own window in full view. Saved automatically.

x.description: Window horizontal position (pixels from left edge of screen).

y.description: Window vertical position (pixels from top edge of screen).

compact_window.description: Position and size of this remote's own window in compact view. Saved automatically.

x.description: Window horizontal position (pixels from left edge of screen).

y.description: Window vertical position (pixels from top edge of screen).

window.description: GUI window position and size. Saved automatically when the GUI is closed, restored on next launch.

x.description: Window horizontal position (pixels from left edge of screen).

y.description: Window vertical position (pixels from top edge of screen).

compact_window.description: GUI compact-view window position and size. Saved automatically when switching to compact mode.

x.description: Window horizontal position (pixels from left edge of screen).

y.description: Window vertical position (pixels from top edge of screen).

view_mode.description: Last active GUI view mode. Restored on next launch.

ui_mode.description: GUI experience: simple (plain words, fewer controls) or advanced (everything). Absent means advanced; onboarding writes simple on a new install.

show_pull_plan.description: Show the plan before Pull all. If omitted, it is on in Simple and off in Advanced.

theme.description: GUI colour theme. Absent means the app follows the operating system.

collapsed.description: GUI layout state: account groups and parent clones folded in the full view, the sidebar rail and the last selected view. Absent means every group and clone is expanded, the sidebar is expanded and the app opens on Needs attention. Keys that no longer exist are pruned on save.

sidebar.description: True when the sidebar is folded to its icon rail. Absent means expanded.

view.description: Last selected view: attention, all, mirrors or account:<account-key>. Absent means Needs attention. A view naming a missing account is pruned on save.

credential_ssh.description: Global SSH platform defaults. Presence indicates SSH is available on this platform.

ssh_folder.description: Path to the SSH configuration directory. Supports ~ prefix. Defaults to ~/.ssh.

credential_gcm.description: Git Credential Manager (HTTPS) platform defaults. Presence indicates GCM is available.

helper.description: Credential helper type. Typically 'manager' for GCM.

credential_store.description: OS-specific credential storage backend. wincredman = Windows Credential Manager, keychain = macOS Keychain, secretservice = Linux GNOME Keyring / KWallet.

credential_token.description: Token/PAT authentication platform defaults. Presence indicates token auth is available. Tokens are stored in ~/.config/gitbox/credentials/.

editors.description: Custom code editors for opening repositories. Auto-detected editors (VS Code, Cursor, Zed) are always included when found on PATH.

name.description: Display name shown in the menu (e.g. 'Sublime Text').

command.description: CLI command to open a folder (e.g. 'subl'). Must be on PATH.

terminals.description: DEPRECATED legacy v2.0 flat list of (terminal-app + shell) entries. Read only to migrate old configs: on load it is converted into terminal_apps + shells + terminal_profiles and dropped. gitbox never writes it.

terminal_apps.description: Terminal emulator applications detected on the host (Windows Terminal, WezTerm, iTerm, gnome-terminal, kitty, alacritty, …) — apps only, independent of the shell. Auto-populated by detection on first run and on every Re-detect; user edits are preserved by id.

id.description: Stable identifier (e.g. 'wt', 'wezterm', 'iterm', 'gnome-terminal'). Used to link from terminal_profiles.

name.description: Display name shown in the Profiles UI (e.g. 'Windows Terminal').

command.description: Resolved absolute path or PATH-relative binary name for the terminal launcher.

args_template.description: Per-app argv template into which a shell + repo path are spliced at launch time. Tokens: {path} = repo path; {shell_command} = the linked Shell.command (omitted when empty); {shell_args} = the linked Shell.args (expands to zero items when empty); {command} = AI-harness argv (legacy).

shells.description: Command-line interpreters available on the host (cmd, powershell, pwsh, git-bash, per-distro WSL, bash, zsh, fish). Detected automatically and merged with user edits.

id.description: Stable identifier (e.g. 'pwsh', 'cmd', 'git-bash', 'wsl-Ubuntu-24-04', 'zsh'). Used to link from terminal_profiles.

command.description: Resolved absolute path or PATH-relative binary for the shell.

args.description: Optional flags passed to the shell (e.g. ['-l'] for login, ['-d', 'Ubuntu-24.04'] for WSL).

terminal_profiles.description: Launchable (terminal × shell) profiles. The profile marked default is the primary action of the per-row 'Open in <terminal>' menu; profiles marked preferred populate the 'Profiles ▸' submenu.

name.description: Display name shown in the menu (e.g. 'Windows Terminal — PowerShell 7').

shell.description: Foreign key into shells[].id. Empty when the terminal handles its own profile selection (e.g. WT --profile).

args.description: Optional explicit argv that REPLACES the linked TerminalApp's args_template at launch time. Used for native-profile terminals (Windows Terminal --profile, iTerm --profile) and for migrated v2.0 entries that carry their own argv.

default.description: Marks this profile as the primary 'Open in <terminal>' action. Exactly one profile should be default; the UI enforces mutex.

preferred.description: Show this profile in the 'Profiles ▸' submenu next to the default action. Hidden when not set.

hidden.description: Suppress this profile from menus. Used to stash auto-detected profiles the user does not want without deleting them (a re-sync would just bring them back).

source.description: Where this profile came from. 'user' profiles can be deleted; auto-detected profiles can only be hidden.

ai_harnesses.description: AI CLI harnesses (claude, codex, agy, aider, agent, opencode, ...) available in the GUI 'Open in' menus. Detected in the background (shortly after launch, every 10 minutes, and when the GUI window regains focus); edit or reorder entries freely. Launches run inside the default Terminal Profile's shell (terminal_profiles[].default).

name.description: Display name shown in the menu (e.g. 'Claude Code').

command.description: Absolute path or command on PATH for the harness binary (e.g. 'claude', '/opt/homebrew/bin/aider').

args.description: Optional extra args passed to the harness (e.g. ['--model', 'sonnet-4.6']). Usually empty.

source.description: Where this entry came from. 'detected' entries were added by the harness sync from the embedded catalog and may have their command re-resolved after a reinstall; 'user' entries are never altered beyond the missing flag. Empty on pre-existing entries until the next sync classifies them.

missing.description: Set by the harness sync when the binary can no longer be found. Missing entries are hidden from menus but kept so a reinstall restores them with their args intact. Cleared automatically when the binary reappears.

accounts.description: Map of account identifiers to account configurations. Each account represents WHO you are on a git server — one unique (hostname, username) pair. The map key is a human-friendly ID (e.g., 'github-personal') also used as the default first-level clone folder.

additionalProperties.description: A Git provider account — identity and credentials for one server login.

provider.description: Git hosting provider type. Determines which API is used for discovery, migration, and mirrors. Use 'generic' for providers without API integration.

url.description: Provider base URL (scheme + host only, no path). E.g., 'https://github.com' or 'https://git.example.org'.

username.description: Account username on the Git provider. Used for authentication and API calls.

name.description: Default git user.name for commits in repos under this account.

email.description: Default git user.email for commits in repos under this account.

default_credential_type.description: Default authentication method for repos in this account. Repos inherit this unless they override it. 'gcm' = Git Credential Manager (HTTPS), 'ssh' = SSH key pair, 'token' = Personal Access Token.

credential_transition.description: Pending credential repair and retirement. Contains artifact identifiers only.

ssh.description: SSH authentication configuration for this account.

host.description: SSH config Host alias (e.g., 'gh-MyGitHubUser'). Used in clone URLs: git@gh-MyGitHubUser:org/repo.git

hostname.description: Real SSH server hostname (e.g., 'github.com'). Written to ~/.ssh/config.

key_type.description: SSH key type to generate. ed25519 is recommended.

gcm.description: Git Credential Manager configuration for this account.

provider.description: GCM provider hint for the OAuth authentication flow.

useHttpPath.description: If true, GCM scopes credentials by full HTTP path (one credential per repo). If false, credentials are shared per domain/user. Maps to git config credential.useHttpPath.

sources.description: Map of source identifiers to source configurations. Each source defines WHAT you clone from an account. The map key is used as the default first-level clone folder (unless overridden by the 'folder' field).

additionalProperties.description: A clone source — references an account and lists repositories to manage.

account.description: References an account key from the 'accounts' section. Defines which credentials and identity to use.

folder.description: Override the first-level clone folder. If omitted, the source map key is used. Path under the source's root.

root.description: The clone root this source clones into, one of global.roots; gitbox remembers the last one picked. If omitted, the default root (the first in global.roots).

repos.description: Map of repository keys to repo configurations. Keys use 'org/repo' format (e.g., 'myorg/my-project', 'MyUser/my-repo'). The org part becomes the second-level folder, the repo part becomes the third-level (clone) folder.

additionalProperties.description: Configuration for a single repository. All fields are optional — repos inherit defaults from the account.

fetch_all_remotes.description: Fetch all configured remotes for this clone. By default Gitbox fetches only origin.

credential_type.description: Override authentication method for this repo. If omitted, inherits from account's default_credential_type.

name.description: Override git user.name for this specific repo.

email.description: Override git user.email for this specific repo.

id_folder.description: Override the second-level directory (org folder). Default: the part before '/' in the repo key. Always relative.

clone_folder.description: Override the third-level directory (clone folder). Default: the part after '/' in the repo key. If absolute (starts with '/' or '~'), replaces the entire clone path, ignoring source folder and id_folder; one starting with '../' replaces it too, relative to the repo's root.

root.description: The clone root this repo lives in, set only when it differs from its source's root.

container.description: Mark this clone as a multi-repo container. gitbox descends into its working tree (up to global.nested_scan_depth, plus every folder its workspace file lists) during discovery to find and onboard nested clones provisioned there by your own tooling. gitbox sets it on its own when the clone root holds a .code-workspace file.

workspace.description: The .code-workspace file, relative to the clone root, that this container opens with in VS Code. gitbox keeps it in step with disk: it records the only file at the root, asks when there are several, and clears it when the file is gone.

workspace_preferred.description: The .code-workspace file I picked among several. Whenever it is at the clone root, the container opens it; while it is missing, another file stands in, and it takes over again, without asking, when it comes back.

mirrors.description: Map of mirror group identifiers to mirror configurations. Each mirror group defines a pair of accounts between which repos are mirrored (push or pull). Mirror repos are NOT cloned locally — they are remote-only backups managed via provider APIs.

additionalProperties.description: A mirror group — pairs two accounts and lists repos mirrored between them.

account_src.description: References an account key from the 'accounts' section. Source account in the mirror pair.

account_dst.description: References an account key from the 'accounts' section. Destination account in the mirror pair. Must differ from account_src.

repos.description: Map of repository keys to mirror repo configurations. Keys use 'org/repo' format matching the repo name on the origin account.

additionalProperties.description: Configuration for a single mirrored repository.

direction.description: Mirror direction. 'push' = origin server pushes to backup. 'pull' = backup server pulls from origin.

origin.description: Which account holds the source of truth. 'src' = account_src, 'dst' = account_dst.

target_repo.description: Full name of the repo on the backup account (e.g., 'org/repo'). Defaults to the same as the map key.

last_sync.description: RFC3339 timestamp of last known successful sync.

error.description: Last error message from setup or sync.
